knowledge:
- key_parameters: k=Number of dimensions to fit (default is 2) ;; round=Logical, whether to round counts (e.g., round = TRUE) ;; confounders=Vector of variable names to condition on to filter out their variability ;; covariates=Vector of constraining variables for constrained RCM ;; responseFun=Shape of the response function in constrained RCM ("linear", "quadratic", or "nonparametric") ;; plotType=Type of plot ("samples", "species", "variables", or combinations like c("species", "samples")) ;; samColour=Variable to color samples (e.g., "Diagnosis", "Shannon", "Deviance", "Age") ;; taxCol=Variable to color taxa (e.g., "Order", "Deviance") ;; taxRegExp=Regular expression to filter taxa in plots ;; taxNum=Number of top taxa to show in biplots/triplots to avoid overplotting ;; returnCoords=Logical, if TRUE returns coordinates for further plotting or projection ;; whichTaxa=For residualPlot, either "response" or "runs" ;; inflVar=Variable to color/size samples by influence on the gradient ;; plotPsi=Axis label metric ("psi", "loglik", or "inertia")
- alternatives: PERMANOVA (via the permanova function) is used as a permutation-based alternative to classical statistical tests for overparametrized models to test cluster significance. phyloseq::estimate_richness is used to calculate richness measures (like Shannon) for sample coloring.
- when_to_use: Use unconstrained RCM as a first step in exploratory analysis to represent all variability in microbiome read count data. Use constrained RCM in a second step to look for variability explained by linear combinations of covariates that maximally separate species niches.
- pitfalls: Do not use non-squared plots (axesFixed = FALSE) as they misrepresent the ordination. Do not perform classical chi-squared tests on deviances because the model is overparametrized. Do not use PERMANOVA to test a subset of grouping variables identified after looking at the ordination plots (it is not designed for post-hoc cluster testing). In constrained RCM with few categorical variables, samples may plot on top of each other; it is best to include all measured sample variables. Be wary of highly influential observations (e.g., a few very young subjects) that strongly affect the ordination. Inertia should be interpreted with caution for overdispersed data as it implicitly assumes the mean to equal the variance.

workflows.name: unconstrained_rcm
workflows.intent: Perform exploratory unconstrained ordination of microbiome read count data, visualize samples and taxa, assess goodness of fit, and test cluster significance.
input: Zeller (phyloseq object containing microbiome read counts and sample metadata)
workflows.stages: 1. Fit unconstrained RCM model (with optional conditioning on confounders) ;; 2. Plot samples, species, or biplots ;; 3. Assess goodness of fit using deviance residuals ;; 4. Test significance of sample clustering using PERMANOVA ;; 5. Extract coordinates and identify top contributing taxa
workflows.code:
# Fitting the unconstrained RCM
ZellerRCM2 = RCM(Zeller, k = 2, round = TRUE)
ZellerRCM3 = RCM(Zeller, k = 3, round = TRUE)
ZellerRCM2cond = RCM(Zeller, k = 2, round = TRUE, confounders = c("Country"))

# Plotting the unconstrained RCM
plot(ZellerRCM2, plotType = "samples")
plot(ZellerRCM2, plotType = "samples", samColour = "Diagnosis")
plot(ZellerRCM2, plotType = "samples", samColour = "Shannon")
plot(ZellerRCM2, plotType = "species")
plot(ZellerRCM2, plotType = "species", taxRegExp = "Fusobacter", taxLabels = TRUE)
plot(ZellerRCM2, plotType = "species", taxLabels = TRUE, taxCol = "Order")
plot(ZellerRCM2, taxNum = 10, samColour = "Diagnosis")

# Adding projections
tmpPlot = plot(ZellerRCM2, taxNum = 10, samColour = "Diagnosis", returnCoords = TRUE)
addOrthProjection(tmpPlot, species = "Alloprevotella tannerae", sample = c(-1.2, 1.5))
plot(ZellerRCM3, Dim = c(1, 3), samColour = "Diagnosis", taxNum = 6)

# Assessing goodness of fit
plot(ZellerRCM2, plotType = "samples", samColour = "Deviance", samSize = 2.5)
plot(ZellerRCM3, plotType = "species", taxCol = "Deviance", samSize = 2.5, Dim = c(1, 2), arrowSize = 0.5)

# Testing significance of clusters using PERMANOVA
permanovaZeller = permanova(ZellerRCM2, "Diagnosis")
permanovaZellerGender = permanova(ZellerRCM2, "Gender", verbose = FALSE)

# Importance of dimensions
plot(ZellerRCM2cond, plotPsi = "psi")
plot(ZellerRCM2cond, plotPsi = "loglik")
plot(ZellerRCM2cond, plotPsi = "inertia")

# Extracting coordinates
zellerCoords = extractCoord(ZellerRCM2)
taxaSignals = rowSums(zellerCoords$species[, c("end1", "end2")]^2)
sortedTaxa = taxa_names(ZellerRCM2$physeq)[order(taxaSignals, decreasing = TRUE)]
sortedTaxa[1:10]

# Non-squared plots
plot(ZellerRCM2, axesFixed = FALSE)

workflows.name: constrained_rcm
workflows.intent: Perform constrained ordination to find variability explained by linear combinations of covariates, using linear or non-parametric response functions.
input: Zeller (phyloseq object containing microbiome read counts and sample metadata)
workflows.stages: 1. Fit constrained RCM model (linear or nonparametric response functions) ;; 2. Plot samples, variables, species-sample biplots, species-variable biplots, or triplots ;; 3. Assess response function fit using residual plots (deviance or Pearson residuals, runs test) ;; 4. Identify influential observations on the environmental gradient
workflows.code:
# Fitting the constrained RCM model
ZellerRCM2constr = RCM(Zeller, k = 2, round = TRUE, covariates = c("Age", "Gender", "BMI", "Country", "Diagnosis"), responseFun = "linear")
ZellerRCM2constrNonParam = RCM(Zeller, round = TRUE, k = 2, covariates = c("Age", "Gender", "BMI", "Country", "Diagnosis"), responseFun = "nonparametric")

# Plotting the constrained RCM model
plot(ZellerRCM2constr, plotType = c("samples"))
plot(ZellerRCM2constr, plotType = c("samples"), samColour = "Diagnosis", samShape = "Country")
plot(ZellerRCM2constr, plotType = "variables")
plot(ZellerRCM2constrNonParam, plotType = "variables")

# Sample-taxon biplot
plot(ZellerRCM2constr, plotType = c("species", "samples"))
tmpPlot2 = plot(ZellerRCM2constr, plotType = c("species", "samples"), returnCoords = TRUE)
addOrthProjection(tmpPlot2, species = "Pseudomonas fluorescens", sample = c(-12, 7))

# Variable-taxon biplot
plot(ZellerRCM2constr, plotType = c("species", "variables"))
tmpPlot3 = plot(ZellerRCM2constr, plotType = c("species", "variables"), returnCoords = TRUE)
addOrthProjection(tmpPlot3, species = "Pseudomonas fluorescens", variable = "DiagnosisSmall_adenoma")

# Triplot
plot(ZellerRCM2constr)

# Non-parametric response function plotting
plotRespFun(ZellerRCM2constrNonParam, taxa = NULL, subdivisions = 50L, yLocVar = c(-30, -50, -75, -62.5, -30, -62.5, -70, -50, -30) * 0.225, Palette = "Set1", angle = 90, yLocSam = -20, axisTitleSize = 16, axisLabSize = 11, legendTitleSize = 18, legendLabSize = 12, samShape = "Diagnosis", labSize = 5)
FusoSpecies = grep("Fusobacterium", value = TRUE, taxa_names(ZellerRCM2constrNonParam$physeq))
plotRespFun(ZellerRCM2constrNonParam, Dim = 1, taxa = FusoSpecies, samShape = "Diagnosis")

# Assessing goodness of fit
residualPlot(ZellerRCM2constr, whichTaxa = "response", numTaxa = 6)
residualPlot(ZellerRCM2constr, whichTaxa = "response", resid = "Pearson", numTaxa = 6)
residualPlot(ZellerRCM2constr, whichTaxa = "runs", resid = "Deviance", numTaxa = 6)

# Identifying influential observations
plot(ZellerRCM2constr, plotType = c("variables", "samples"), inflVar = "Age")
plot(ZellerRCM2constr, plotType = c("variables", "samples"), samColour = "Age")
plot(ZellerRCM2constr, plotType = c("variables", "samples"), inflVar = "Age", Influence = TRUE, inflDim = 2)
plot(ZellerRCM2constr, plotType = c("variables", "samples"), inflVar = "DiagnosisNormal", samShape = "Diagnosis")
plot(ZellerRCM2, plotType = "samples", samSize = 2.5, inflVar = "psi")
plot(ZellerRCM2constr, plotType = "samples", samSize = 2.5, inflVar = "psi")

# Constrained RCM with few variables
ZellerRCM3constr = RCM(Zeller, k = 2, round = TRUE, covariates = c("Gender", "Diagnosis"), responseFun = "linear")
plot(ZellerRCM3constr, plotType = "samples", samColour = "Diagnosis", samShape = "Country")
